newsitem.title: TURKEY: Moody's may cut Turkey credit rating, paper says.
newsitem.headline: Moody's may cut Turkey credit rating, paper says.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service may downgrade Turkey's Ba3 sovereign credit rating because of a deteriorating fiscal position, high inflation and political uncertainty, the Turkish daily Milliyet reported on Friday.
The paper quoted an unnamed senior Moody's official as saying that the agency would probably cut Turkey's rating.
Moody's in London said it had no comment on the newspaper report.
"It is discouraging that the government has no medium term reform policy," the paper quoted the official as saying.
The official said Turkey's main economic problem was big budget deficits, adding that the country was in need of a tax reform to improve its inefficient taxation system.
Moody's last month placed under review for possible downgrade Turkey's Ba3 long-term foreign currency sovereign ceiling for bonds, and its B1 foreign currency sovereign ceiling for bank deposits.
Turkish bankers say the agency may downgrade Turkey's credit rating in late February or early March.
They said the markets had largely discounted any downgrading.

Standard and Poor's cut Turkey's long term foreign currency rating in December to B from B+ in a move which it said reflected worsening fiscal and debt service pressures. -- Istanbul Newsroom, 90-212-275 0875
